subject: [PATCH v2] mm/huge_memory: prevent losing PG_waiters in __split_folio_to_order()

reviews.author: Zi Yan
reviews.summary:
Reviewer Zi Yan noted that prep_compound_page() writing PG_head after clear_compound_head() breaks the page flags visibility requirement, and suggested building the whole flags word for the new head, including PG_head, before smp_wmb().

Reviewer Zi Yan suggested using data_race() to handle the potential race condition when setting PG_head on new_folio, as the flags are stable at this moment.

Reviewer Zi Yan noted that setting PG_head atomically on its own breaks the ordering requirement that page flags must be visible before the page becomes non-compound, and suggested building the whole flags word for the new head, including PG_head, and storing it once before smp_wmb().
reviews.raw_body:
At that time, I did not think about separate __SetPageHead() and
__prep_compound_page() and what I had in mind would still call
prep_compound_page() after clear_compound_head(). That was the source
of the complication.

But your version does not have the issue.

---

I am planning to use data_race() like I said in Ye Liu’s email, since
the flags are stable at this moment. But let me know if I miss something.

---

Best Regards,
Yan, Zi

2026-11-09.patch_summary: This patch fixes a bug in the __split_folio_to_order() function where PG_waiters could be lost when splitting a compound page. The problem arises from setting PG_head after clear_compound_head(), which breaks the ordering requirement that page flags must be visible before the page becomes non-compound. To fix this, the patch builds the whole flags word for the new head, including PG_head, and stores it once before smp_wmb(). This approach ensures that PG_waiters are preserved during the split operation.
